title: Coefficient extension of local Frobenius through the specified point comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb/\Ql$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$, with geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. All coefficient categories are the raw rationalized constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and Weil pairs and their morphisms are those of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the specified natural pullback-composition and pullback/scalar comparisons, rationalized with their equality-of-morphisms and finite-iteration compatibilities, of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

Let $F\subset L$ be finite subextensions of $\Qlb/\Ql$, write $T_U(M)=M\otimes_F L$ on $U=X,s$, and write $T_{\mathrm{pt}}(C)=C\otimes_F L$ on ordinary point complexes. Let $n\geq1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ with geometric point $\bar x:s\to X$. For $H=F,L$ put $P_H=L\bar x_H^*$, $Q_H=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,H}$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $D_H=Q_HP_H$, $G_{H,r}=L(g_X^r)_H^*$ and $S_{H,r}=L(g_s^r)_H^*$. Let
$$a_{r,M}:T_XG_{F,r}M\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{L,r}T_XM$$
be the specified pullback/scalar comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with normalization as above. Write
$$b_M:D_F(M)\otimes_F L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_L(T_XM)$$
for the inverse rationalized point-sections scalar comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] followed by $Q_L$ of the specified pullback/scalar comparison for $\bar x$. For a Weil pair $(M,\theta)$ over $F$, put $M^T=T_XM$ and $\theta_L=T_X(\theta)a_{1,M}^{-1}$. Use the iterated Weil maps and point transports of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] and [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural]. For $H=F,L$ let
$$\rho_{H,N}:S_{H,n}P_HN\xrightarrow{\sim}P_HG_{H,n}N,\quad R_H(N)=Q_H(\rho_{H,N})I_{P_HN}^{[n]},$$
where $\rho$ uses $g_X^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$.

The maps $b_M$ are natural isomorphisms for all morphisms of $D^b_c(X,F)$: for every $v:M\to M'$,
$$b_{M'}(D_F(v)\otimes_F L)=D_L(T_Xv)b_M.$$
For every $F$-Weil pair $(M,\theta)$ their iterated structure maps satisfy
$$\theta_L^{[r]}a_{r,M}=T_X(\theta^{[r]})\quad(r\geq1).$$
For every $M\in D^b_c(X,F)$ the return transports satisfy
$$D_L(a_{n,M})b_{G_{F,n}M}(R_F(M)\otimes_F L)=R_L(M^T)b_M.$$
The local operators $\mathcal F_{H,x,n}(N,\eta)=D_H(\eta^{[n]})R_H(N)$ therefore satisfy
$$b_M(\mathcal F_{F,x,n}(M,\theta)\otimes_F L)=\mathcal F_{L,x,n}(M^T,\theta_L)b_M.$$
All assertions apply to the full constructible Weil-pair domain, with no integral Weil-stable lattice or finite-Tor condition on finite reductions. For $F=L$, $b_M$ is the identity under the specified unit identifications.
